confidence_notes: I ran four web searches. One found the RBA rate. Three checked food and drink prices in Penang using aggregated cost-of-living sites (Numbeo, CityCost, My Life Elsewhere, Expatistan) and a few local guides. To get USD values I assumed about 4.2 MYR per USD; I did not search for that rate. Coffee (about RM12) and inexpensive meals (about RM10-20) are fairly well supported. Beer is based on local draught at about RM17 a pint, with a range of RM10-30. Penang alcohol prices are high for Southeast Asia because of Malaysian excise duty. The mid-range dinner for two is my estimate of about RM105-115. The sources were scattered and partly old, including an Expatistan figure of about RM136 for an Italian dinner for two with wine. I found almost no direct price data for cocktails, so that estimate (about RM38-42) comes mainly from local beer prices and the high-duty market. Wine is based on a 2023 house-wine price of RM16, which is probably out of date, plus the beer-price relationship; I estimate about RM30-33 a glass. Both are less certain. All four accommodation anchors are general estimates from model knowledge for George Town in July. I did not search for accommodation prices or check booking sites, so they are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Main basis: aggregated cost-of-living data for Penang (George Town). I compared these with Kuala Lumpur and Malacca, which have similar Malaysian alcohol excise and hawker-food prices, and with mid-sized heritage tourist cities in Southeast Asia for accommodation.
